sections.ta:
அஞ்சாவென் நெஞ்சம் துடிக்கிறது கேசவா
வஞ்சமோவென மருள்கிறது காலும் நடுங்குகிறது
நாலும் தெரிந்த நீயோ நாவடைத்து நிற்கின்றாய்
வெற்றி முரசு கேட்கவில்லை தோற்றம் யாவும் வற்றியதே
என்னுளம் நிறை மன்னுபுகழ் மைந்தன் எங்கே
sections.translit:
anjAven nenjam thudikkiRadhu kEsavA
vanjamOvena maruLgiRadhu kAlum nadungugiRadhu
nAlum therindha nIyO nAvadaitthu niRkindRAy
vetRi murasu kEtkavillai thOtRam yAvum vatRiyadhE
ennuLam niRai mannupugazh maindhan engE
sections.en: விருத்தம் (viruttham) Arjuna addresses Krishna: My typically brave heart is beating fast. I am scared that there was deceit on the battlefield today. My legs are trembling. You, Kesava, have tremendous foresight and yet you are not uttering a single word. There is no usual drum beating for the day’s victory in our camp. Everything looks dry and there is no excitement on anyone’s face. My beloved, illustrious son will run towards me to brief me about the day’s proceedings. Where is he?

sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
விதியோ அது செய்த சதியோ இதுவும்
மதியோ தந்தை இருக்க தனயன் மாய்வதும்
sections.translit:
vidhiyO adhu seydha sadhiyO idhuvum
madhiyO thandhai irukka thanayan mAyvadhum
sections.en: Is this fate or is it a wicked scheme? Is it proper for a young child to die while the father is alive?

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
ஆண்டுகள் பல கழிந்து உனைக் கண்டு மகிழுங்கால்
மாண்டது ஏன் மகனே தருணத்தே நான் கைவிடுத்ததுமேன்
sections.translit:
ANdugaL pala kazhindhu unaik kaNdu magizhungkAl
mANdadhu En maganE tharuNatthE nAn kaividutthadhumEn
sections.en: I have not seen you for years. I thought I was finally going to have happy times with you. Why did you die, my son? Why did I abandon you and leave you to defend yourself at the right moment?

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
சூழ்ந்தனர் கௌரவர் என்றபின்னே தர்மமும்
வீழ்ந்தது அன்றோ ஈன்ற தாயை உன் இல்லாளை
பிறவா மகவை எங்கண் காண்பேனோ தேற்றுவேனோ
உறவா இவரென உடன் பிறந்தோரைத் தூற்றுவேனோ
sections.translit:
sUzhndhanar kauravar endRapinnE dharmamum
vIzhndhadhu andRO IndRa thAyai un illALai
piRavA magavai engaN kANbEnO thEtRuvEnO
uRavA ivarena udan piRandhOraith thUtRuvEnO
sections.en: I heard the news that the Kauravas surrounded you. Isn’t it true that righteousness fell at that moment? How will I look at your mother, young wife, and your offspring now and offer them my sympathies? Or will I find fault with my brothers and curse them, for not helping you at a time when you needed it badly?
sections.label: விருத்தம்(viruttham)
ta

துஷ்கர்மா ஜெயத்ரதா சோதரர் நால்வரையும்
குலக் கொழுந்தை அண்ட விடாதுத் தடுத்தாய்
பாலனுக்குக் காலன் ஆன மூடனே என்னுரை கேள்
சரம் நூறு பொழிவேன் சிரம் தனைக் கொய்வேன்
குருதி கொட்ட நினை வதைப்பேன் இது உறுதியடா
sections.translit:
dhushkarmA jayadhrathA sOdharar nAlvaraiyum
Kulak kozhundhai aNda vidAdhuth thadutthAy
bAlanukkuk kAlan Ana mUdanE ennurai kEL
saram nURu pozhivEn siram thanaik koyvEn
kurudhi kotta ninai vadhaippEn idhu uRudhiyadA
sections.en: Arjuna curses Jayadhrata and takes an oath: Evil Jayadhrata, you deliberately blocked my brothers from Abhimanyu as they sought to protect my offspring. You became the god of death for a young boy. Listen to me, fool: I will shoot hundreds of arrows and decapitate you. I will kill you, you will soak in blood. This is certain.

notes: This song was written for Abhinaya Dance Company’s Dance Program titled : “Arjuna, A warrior’s Tale”, November 15, 2014. Mexican Heritage Theater Plaza, 1700 Alum Rock Ave, San Jose, CA. Rasika Kumar as Arjuna laments Abhimanyu’s demise in the scene. The song is based on the scene from the thirteenth day of the Kurukshetra war between Pandavas and Kauravas. Yudhishtra sent Abhimanyu, Arjuna’s son, to stop Dronacharya from fiercely attacking. Young Abhimanyu fought like a lion and caused heavy damage to the Kaurava army. The Sindhu king, Jayadhrata, had an evil plan. He instructed the Kaurava army to keep the Pandava brothers engaged in war so that they could not save Abhimanyu. Arjuna was elsewhere with Krishna fighting a different army based on a plan set by Drona, the commander of the Kauravas. Abhimanyu broke into the chakravyuh or encirclement of the Kaurava army. Unfortunately, Arjuna did not teach him how to get out of a chakravyuh. Seasoned warriors from the opposing army surrounded Abhimanyu, and Dushasana’s son hit him with a mace and killed him. At the end of the day, Arjuna walked with Krishna. He told Krishna that he felt uneasy for unknown reasons and worried about whether his brothers were safe. Krishna with all his foresight did not say a word about what happened to Abhimanyu. Nearing their camp, Arjuna did not hear any triumphant drumming. Nor did Abhimanyu run to him and embrace him. He concluded that something tragic had occurred to the Pandava army. Arjuna learnt that Jayadhrata used his power to hold enemies for a single day in a war (a boon from Lord Siva that excluded Krishna and Arjuna) so that the Kauravas could kill the lonely Abhimanyu. Jayadhrata also kicked the dead body to check if the young warrior was slain or not. Learning all of the details surrounding his son’s death, Arjuna vowed to kill the evil Jayadhrata before the next day ended. Arjuna swore that he would kill himself if he did not accomplish his goal. The following references provide details: Arjuna singles out Jayadhrata for Abhimanyu’s death and takes a vow Mahabharata, C. Rajagopalachari, 1985, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, Kulapati K.M. Munshi Marg, Bombay 400007, Chapter LXXIX, LXXX, LXXXI Pages 247 – 256. ஶ்ரீ மஹாபாரத ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, பதின்மூன்றாவது நாள் போர், பக்கம் 780 – 783.
